RaMP multi-database ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) assigns FDR = 6.05e-18 to both the SMPDB 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' pathway (SMPDB:SMP00068) and the KEGG 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' pathway (KEGG:map00150), with 6 of the 10 input metabolites hitting a 27-member pathway roster (fold enrichment 1 501×). react_result.final_narrative_text: Three orthogonal pathway-analysis paradigms converge on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant biological signature in the treatment group. RaMP multi-database ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) assigns FDR = 6.05e-18 to both the SMPDB 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' pathway (SMPDB:SMP00068) and the KEGG 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' pathway (KEGG:map00150), with 6 of the 10 input metabolites hitting a 27-member pathway roster (fold enrichment 1 501×). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returns the parent KEGG hsa00140 'Steroid hormone biosynthesis' as rank-1 (p = 5.77e-7) with the same 6 steroids as hits. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis corroborates this at p = 4.2e-4 with its 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' module (MUMM pathway), where all five input steroids are confirmed in the network overlap. The six driver metabolites — 17β-estradiol (KEGG:C00951), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), estrone (KEGG:C00468), dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), and dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227) — cover the full androgen-to-estrogen conversion axis. Aromatase (CYP19A1, gene R01488) is the canonical enzyme mediating the androstenedione→estrone step; 17β-HSD and AKR1C family enzymes interconvert estrone/estradiol and androstenedione/testosterone. The four non-steroid metabolites (N-acetylgalactosamine, coumarin, xanthine, β-mercaptoethanol) show no consistent pathway enrichment across methods, indicating they are likely peripheral or context-specific hits. The convergence of ORA statistical significance, m/z network topology, and KEGG pathway geometry across three independent tools strongly implicates systemic perturbation of steroidogenesis as the primary biological effect of the treatment.

  "narrative_text": "Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological domain: steroid hormone homeostasis. A multi-database ORA via RaMP (SMPDB + KEGG + Reactome + WikiPathways), an empirical-compound m/z network analysis via mummichog (human_mfn), and a KEGG-specific PSEA via MetaboAnalystR all rank steroid-related pathways as the top hit with extremely low p-values and high fold-enrichment. RaMP additionally returns the Reactome entries R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) and R-HSA-193144 (Estrogen biosynthesis), both with FDR < 5 × 10⁻¹³. The WikiPathways entry WP:WP496 (Steroid biosynthesis) also appears with 5/5 steroid hits and fold-enrichment > 2800. The remaining four input metabolites — N-acetylgalactosamine, coumarin, xanthine, and beta-mercaptoethanol — do not participate in steroid biosynthesis and were not captured by the top steroid-enrichment pathways across any tool, consistent with the biological interpretation that the treatment group is characterised primarily by altered sex-steroid flux. Androstenedione (a 19-carbon androgen intermediate) and estrone (its aromatisation product) are the most connected nodes in the overlapping androgen / estrogen network and are the canonical substrate and product of CYP19A1 (aromatase). The RaMP ORA reports six out of six possible steroid input metabolites as hits within hsa00140, yielding a raw p-value of 5.77 × 10⁻⁷, confirming that the steroid sub-system is the dominant signal in this dataset. Limitations: three tools were unavailable (FELLA runtime error; sspa module missing; query_pathway_members does not index KEGG), reducing cross-validation depth.   "narrative_text": "Three complementary enrichment paradigms converged on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP-DB ORA returned the multi-database consensus pathway 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150) with FDR = 6.0×10⁻¹⁸, fold enrichment 1501, and six steroid input metabolites mapped (androstenedione, estrone, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, 17β-estradiol, dehydroepiandrosterone). A second independent ORA via MetaboAnalystR confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as the top KEGG-only hit (p = 5.77×10⁻⁷, 6/87 pathway metabolites overlapped). The m/z-direct mummichog analysis independently surfaced 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p = 1.68×10⁻⁴) and 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p = 4.20×10⁻⁴) as ranks 1 and 2, with 14-15 overlapping metabolites including all six steroid inputs plus predicted intermediates. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converged on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP-DB ORA returned the multi-database consensus pathway 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150) with FDR = 6.0×10⁻¹⁸, fold enrichment 1501, and six steroid input metabolites mapped (androstenedione, estrone, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, 17β-estradiol, dehydroepiandrosterone). A second independent ORA via MetaboAnalystR confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as the top KEGG-only hit (p = 5.77×10⁻⁷, 6/87 pathway metabolites overlapped). The m/z-direct mummichog analysis independently surfaced 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p = 1.68×10⁻⁴) and 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p = 4.20×10⁻⁴) as ranks 1 and 2, with 14-15 overlapping metabolites including all six steroid inputs plus predicted intermediates. The cross-paradigm consensus is therefore robust: six C18/C19 steroid hormones were differentially between treatment and control. Three non-steroid inputs (coumarin, N-acetylgalactosamine, xanthine, beta-mercaptoethanol) did not enrich in any steroid pathway and likely represent independent signals or assay noise. The driver metabolite set is the six shared hits (androstenedione, estrone, testosterone, DHT, 17β-estradiol, DHEA), spanning both the androgen and estrogen arms of the pathway.
